name: Lake Everstill
summary: Lake Everstill is the expansive azure body of water dominating the heart of the Redridge Mountains, flanking the town of Lakeshire. Once celebrated for tranquil fishing and clean mountain runoff, its shores and waters have lately turned treacherous due to aggressive murloc tribes and predatory lake beasts.

sections.title: Heart of the Valley
sections.body: Spanning the central basin of Redridge, Lake Everstill provides the scenic backdrop and vital waterway for the township of Lakeshire. Its crystal-clear waters drain eastward toward the looming heights of Stonewatch. Spanned by the town's central bridge, the lake has long sustained local trade and quiet anglers, though anyone walking the shoreline today will find its peaceful reputation thoroughly shattered by encroaching wilderness threats.

sections.title: Trouble in the Depths
sections.body: In recent times, hostile murlocs have established camps along the northern and eastern shallows, disrupting trade and harrying fishermen. Below the surface, aquatic hazards lurk as well, including dangerous threshers that patrol the deeper waters.

faq.q: What dangerous creatures live in Lake Everstill?
faq.answer: The shallows are crawling with hostile murloc tribes, including scouts, tidecallers, and flesheaters. Swimming deeper poses its own hazards, as giant threshers and aggressive muckdwellers patrol beneath the surface.

faq.q: Where does the water from Lake Everstill flow?
faq.answer: The lake is drained by an eastern river that flows out past the slopes beneath the Blackrock-held stronghold of Stonewatch.

faq.q: Can you fish safely in Lake Everstill?
aliases: is it safe to fish lakeshire
faq.answer: While the waters teem with catfish and sagefish, fishing has become extremely dangerous. Murloc raiding parties camp right along the water's edge, and large threshers attack anyone straying too far into the deep.

angles.text: Mages passing through Lakeshire will find the lake's troubles mundane rather than arcane: murloc camps choke the shallows while threshers patrol the deeper waters.
Controlling the lake and its crossings is vital for Lakeshire's survival against the coordinated incursions of Redridge murlocs and nearby Blackrock orcs.
